title: MIDILM: Controllable Text-to-MIDI Generation
heroSub: Dual-Path Model for Controllable Symbolic Music Generation
overview: A dual-path model that generates controllable symbolic music (MIDI) from text prompts. It turns conditions written in natural language into musical structure, and was accepted to the 40th AAAI (2026) Main Track. (Shuyu Li*, Dooho Choi*, Yunsick Sung, *co-first authors)
roles: Co-designed the dual-path decoder with modality isolation: text and MIDI tokens share one masked self-attention stack, then split into a dedicated MLP path for text and a MoE path (8 experts per layer, top-2 routing) for musical structure.

Implemented the training pipeline with the combined objective of cross-entropy and a MoE load-balancing loss, and trained the 12-layer decoder with rotary positional encoding on MidiCaps (168K text-MIDI pairs, REMI+ 515-token vocabulary).
Ran the evaluation on semantic and structural metrics (CLAP, CLaMP 3, TB/TBT, CK/CKD, CR), where MIDILM beat the strongest baseline by 6.07% on CLAP up to 144.77% on TB.
Filed two patents based on this work (Symbolic Music Generation Method and Device 10-2025-0139998, Symbolic Music Prediction Model Training Method 10-2025-0139997).
Selected as a top-100 team (of 630) in the AI Champion Program, and exhibited and presented the framework at 2025 AI Festa (COEX).
skills: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Language Models
Symbolic music (MIDI) representation and tokenization, conditional generation

title: PixTention: Dynamic Pixel-Level Adapter
period: Image and Vision Computing (IF 4.7), 163:105746 · First author · 2025
overview: A PEFT study that proposes a dynamic pixel-level adapter guided by attention maps. Unlike common adapters that act on the whole image in the same way, it changes the adapter strength by region and improves generation quality. Published in Image and Vision Computing (IF 4.7) as first author. (Dooho Choi, Yunsick Sung)
roles: AS-IS: existing adapter-based PEFT applies the same update to every region of an image, which limits expressiveness when regions need different levels of adaptation.

TO-BE: designed and implemented a structure that reads region importance from attention maps and controls the adapter at the pixel level. Led the whole project as first author, from the idea to experiments and writing.
skills: PyTorch, diffusion and vision models, attention analysis
Adapter and PEFT design, quantitative and qualitative evaluation

title: LoRA Fusion: Enhancing Image Generation
heroSub: Better image generation by combining multiple LoRAs
overview: A study on combining multiple LoRAs to improve image generation. It tackles the quality drop that appears when LoRAs trained on different concepts are used together. Published in MDPI Mathematics (IF 2.4). (Dooho Choi*, Jeonghyeon Im*, Yunsick Sung, *co-first authors)
roles: Designed and implemented the LoRA fusion method and ran the experiments as a co-first author.
Ran quantitative and qualitative quality comparisons on Stable Diffusion and wrote the paper.
This work started the PEFT-based generation research line that continued into PixTention and MIDILM.
skills: Image generation metrics and experiment design
